activities.anchor: The world's religious landscape is the data
activities.caption: call the combined adherent count
activities.name: porAdherentEst

config.prompt: Christianity has about 2.4 billion adherents and Islam about 1.9 billion. Roughly how many is that together?
config.why: About 4.3 billion — and they differ structurally, not just doctrinally: some theistic, some non-theistic, some polytheistic-and-monist at once, some organised around law rather than creed. A philosopher who knows only one tradition is arguing with half the evidence in.

activities.anchor: all religions are basically the same
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a comparativist briefing
activities.name: porFlattenSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on comparison is wrong — click it:
lines: Buddhism's non-self and Advaita's non-dualism contradict the personal creator theism assumes.
Judaism's covenantal law, Christian grace and Buddhist karma are different problem-solutions, not synonyms.
Each tradition identifies a different core problem — sin, suffering, pride, ignorance — and a different cure (Prothero, 2010).
The differences are just different names for one ethical core, so the pluralist paraphrase holds.
config.correction: The pluralist paraphrase is comfortable and false — the traditions themselves reject the flattening, and honest comparison holds the differences at full strength.
config.why: Holding differences at full strength is exactly what makes comparison worth doing.

activities.anchor: The methodological toolkit keeps the discipline honest
activities.caption: pair each method with what it does
activities.name: porMethodMatch

config.prompt: The methods of comparison — pair each with its move:

pairs.right: brackets truth-questions to describe experience from within

config.why: Comparison stays honest only when each description is labelled with the method that produced it — always ask whose description, and for what purpose.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the discipline's standing
activities.name: porClientCloze

config.text: The discipline argues in both directions at full strength: Mackie and Rowe are as canonical as Plantinga. Apologetics is advocacy with a %%0%%; philosophy of religion has %%1%%.
config.hint: Whom does apologetics serve — and whom does philosophy of religion serve?

activities.anchor: The tradition's philosophical depth is chronologically layered
activities.caption: order the philosophical layers
activities.name: porVedaOrder

config.prompt: Hinduism's philosophical depth is layered — put the layers in order:
items: the Rig Veda's oldest hymns (roughly 1500–1200 BCE)
the Upanishads supply the classical metaphysics: atman and Brahman (roughly 800–300 BCE)
Shankara's Advaita — rigorous non-dualism (about the 8th century CE)
Ramanuja's qualified non-dualism keeps a personal God (11th–12th century)
the later bhakti of Kabir and Mirabai — devotion over caste and ritual
config.why: The six darshanas formalise the debates between; by its own lights the tradition is both polytheist and monist — many deities as forms of one reality — which is why the category 'polytheism' misfires on it.

activities.caption: pair each concept with its metaphysics
activities.name: porBuddhaMatch

config.prompt: Buddhism's philosophical schools — pair each with its claim:

pairs.right: no persistent self — the person is a causally connected process, not a substance
all phenomena are empty of inherent existence — by tetralemma
postpones final nirvana to liberate others

config.why: Fully religious — ritual, community, liberation — and non-theistic: Buddhism is the standing counterexample to 'religion requires God'.

events.title: Plantinga's free-will defence
events.text: meets the logical version — arguably victorious as stated

events.title: Rowe's fawn
events.text: the evidential version — gratuitous suffering remains theism's hardest case

activities.anchor: Faith and reason: the epistemology tier
activities.caption: walk the epistemic standards
activities.name: porTierBranch

config.root: Beneath the arguments sits the epistemology tier: what does belief in God need? You hold a belief the evidence cannot settle.

start.text: Which epistemic standard are you applying?

choices.label: Evidentialism (Clifford, 1877)
choices.feedback: Then belief waits: 'it is wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone, to believe anything upon insufficient evidence.'

choices.label: James's 'The Will to Believe' (1896)
choices.feedback: Then a right to choose — precisely where the evidence is genuinely undecidable and the option is forced and momentous.

choices.label: Reformed epistemology (Plantinga)
choices.feedback: Then no obligation to argue first: theistic belief can be 'properly basic', grounded in experience directly, like belief in other minds.

end.text: Fideism would refuse reason's court altogether. Which standard is right is itself the live dispute — the tier explains the field's stalemate.

config.why: The arguments are assessed against different epistemic standards — that is where the real dispute about faith and reason lives.
